guarantees.claim: When key_dec_sel equals KEY_DEC_EXPAND, key_dec_d is assigned key_expand_out.
When key_dec_sel equals KEY_DEC_CLEAR, key_dec_d is assigned key_expand_out.
In all other cases (default), key_dec_d is assigned prd_clearing_key_i.
guarantees.cond: key_dec_sel is not KEY_DEC_EXPAND and not KEY_DEC_CLEAR

assumptions.claim: key_dec_sel must be driven only with defined key-selection values (KEY_DEC_EXPAND, KEY_DEC_CLEAR) during normal operation.
assumptions.risk: If key_dec_sel takes an unexpected value (e.g., FSM error or glitch), key_dec_d will be sourced from prd_clearing_key_i, potentially loading a clearing or random key value, breaking decryption or compromising key secrecy.

uncertain_points.claim: KEY_DEC_EXPAND and KEY_DEC_CLEAR both select the same source key_expand_out; the reason for two distinct modes with identical data is not evident from this block.
uncertain_points.risk: If the modes were intended to use different sources for different phases, this may cause incorrect key derivation, weakening security or producing wrong decryption results.

uncertain_points.claim: The default case selects prd_clearing_key_i; whether this acts as a secure fallback clearing value or as a potentially weak/inappropriate key source is unclear.
uncertain_points.risk: If prd_clearing_key_i is a known weak value, its inadvertent use could expose secret material or lead to predictable decryption. If it is meant as a clearing constant, using it in active operation could corrupt key state.

uncertain_points.claim: No error flag is raised when key_dec_sel falls to default; downstream logic may use prd_clearing_key_i without detection.
uncertain_points.risk: A fault in the controlling FSM could silently load the wrong key, causing silent data corruption or security bypass with no alert.
